Answer: B
Reason: The clinical history of dry heaving and stifled sneeze in a young male, combined with radiographic findings of linear lucencies along the hilar/paratracheal regions and subcutaneous emphysema, is classic for spontaneous pneumomediastinum caused by alveolar rupture (Macklin effect). Esophageal perforation typically presents with more severe systemic toxicity and pleural effusions, while traumatic pneumothorax would show a visible visceral pleural line and lung collapse.
